provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Picks out an extreme or unexpected case, 'even X', on a noun or case particle (子供だって, 先生にだって), and plain 'too' with a person (私だって行きたい). Three siblings share the string: hearsay news (臨時休業だって), a rising-tone question checking what you heard (校庭だって？), and 'even if' on a ta-stem verb (呼んだって). Clause-initial だって is a separate conjunction, 'because; but' (だって、時間がないもん), covered by no entry here.

examples.ruby: 子供[こども]だってそんな話[はなし]は信[しん]じないよ。
examples.english: Even a kid wouldn't buy a story like that.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]にだって分[わ]からない問題[もんだい]がある。
examples.english: There are problems even a teacher can't solve.

examples.ruby: 東京[とうきょう]からだって日帰[ひがえ]りで行[い]けるよ。
examples.english: You can get there and back in a day even from Tokyo.

patterns.usage_note: Offers a noun as a representative case rather than the most extreme one: even this much is enough (素人でも組み立てられる). Register-neutral between casual だって and bookish すら, and alone in this group it also floats a casual suggestion (お茶でも飲みませんか), where さえ and すら are impossible. After a て-form, 〜てでも means 'even if it takes doing that' (借金をしてでも).

examples.ruby: 素人[しろうと]でも三十分[さんじゅっぷん]あれば組[く]み立[た]てられる。
examples.english: Even a beginner can put it together in thirty minutes.

examples.ruby: お茶[ちゃ]でも飲[の]みながら話[はな]しませんか。
examples.english: How about we talk over a cup of tea or something?

examples.ruby: 借金[しゃっきん]をしてでもあの車[くるま]が欲[ほ]しい。
examples.english: I want that car badly enough to go into debt for it.

patterns.usage_note: Names the case least likely to hold, so everything more likely follows from it (食事さえ取る暇がない, 五月にさえ雪が降る). Sharper than でも and typical where the situation is bad or surprising; すら is the bookish equivalent. It alone forms the sufficient-condition frame さえ〜ば, 'if only X' (天気さえ良ければ). でさえ is the usual shape when the marked element is a subject or a copular predicate (専門家でさえ間違える).

examples.ruby: 忙[いそが]しくて食事[しょくじ]さえ取[と]る暇[ひま]がない。
examples.english: I'm so busy I don't even have time to eat.

examples.ruby: 北海道[ほっかいどう]では五月[ごがつ]にさえ雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]ることがある。
examples.english: In Hokkaido it can snow even in May.

examples.ruby: 天気[てんき]さえ良[よ]ければ、明日[あした]は出発[しゅっぱつ]できる。
examples.english: As long as the weather holds, we can set out tomorrow.

patterns.usage_note: Names the least likely case as さえ does, and very often pairs with a negative (名前すら思い出せない, 議題にすら上らなかった). The register is written and formal, including narration and speeches; さえ is the default in conversation. It does not enter the さえ〜ば conditional.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]は熱[ねつ]が高[たか]くて、私[わたし]の名前[なまえ]すら思[おも]い出[だ]せなかった。
examples.english: My grandmother's fever was so high she couldn't even remember my name.

examples.ruby: その提案[ていあん]は議題[ぎだい]にすら上[のぼ]らなかった。
examples.english: The proposal never even made it onto the agenda.

examples.ruby: 当時[とうじ]の政府[せいふ]は事実[じじつ]の公表[こうひょう]すら拒[こば]んだ。
examples.english: The government of the day refused even to make the facts public.
